## Teaching points

1. Trismus, unilateral palatal swelling and a muffled voice suggest quinsy. Arrange urgent specialist assessment.
2. Assess the airway first and repeat the assessment if symptoms change.
3. Poor intake may require IV hydration and parenteral therapy; an oral prescription alone does not solve this presentation.
4. Specialist drainage and definitive source control are not replaced by a transient reduction in pain or temperature.
